story.title: Two generations. One coffee legacy.
story.body1: Birra Group General Trading PLC was established in 2004 by a team of young entrepreneurs from a coffee-farming family, with two generations of production behind them.
story.body2: That family brings roughly 30 years as local suppliers and 15 years as exporters — deep-rooted knowledge of Ethiopian coffee, applied to international markets.

origin.title: Seven origins, one birthplace of Arabica

regions.name: Yirgacheffe
regions.subtitle: SOUTHERN ETHIOPIA
regions.description: A wet-processed coffee considered the best high-grown coffee in southern Ethiopia. Slow growth at altitude gives bright acidity, clean intense taste and complex floral aroma, sometimes with berry, wine or citrus undertones.

regions.name: Sidamo
regions.subtitle: SOUTHERN ETHIOPIA
regions.description: Grown across high plateaus south of Yirgacheffe, Sidamo lots range from washed to sun-dried natural, giving a winey, complex cup with berry sweetness and a full body.

regions.name: Guji
regions.subtitle: SOUTHERN OROMIA
regions.description: A newer designation neighbouring Yirgacheffe and Sidamo, Guji lots are prized for their floral aroma, stone-fruit sweetness and delicate, tea-like body.

regions.name: Harrar
regions.subtitle: EASTERN ETHIOPIA
regions.description: Grown on dry highland terraces east of Addis Ababa and traditionally sun-dried, Harrar delivers a wild, wine-like character with notes of blueberry and dark chocolate.

regions.name: Limmu
regions.subtitle: WESTERN ETHIOPIA
regions.description: Washed lots from the forested highlands of western Oromia, Limmu coffee is well balanced with winey acidity, spice notes and a clean, rounded finish.

regions.name: Jimma
regions.subtitle: SOUTHWESTERN ETHIOPIA
regions.description: One of Ethiopia's largest producing zones, Jimma yields both washed and natural lots with a mild acidity, earthy body and approachable, everyday character.

regions.name: Nekemte
regions.subtitle: WESTERN ETHIOPIA
regions.description: Grown in the Wollega zone, Nekemte lots are typically naturally processed, producing a fruit-forward, wine-like cup with notes of chocolate and dried fruit.

journey.title: Eight stages between a cherry and your cup

stages.title: Farm
stages.desc: Grown by smallholder farms and cooperatives across seven Ethiopian regions.

stages.title: Harvest
stages.desc: Selective hand-picking, red cherry only, delivered to the nearest station the same afternoon.

stages.title: Processing
stages.desc: Depulped and fermented, or dried on raised beds — decided lot by lot against the buyer contract.

stages.title: Drying
stages.desc: Sun-dried on raised beds or patios, turned by hand and monitored until target moisture is reached.

stages.title: Milling & Hulling
stages.desc: Parchment and dried skin removed, beans cleaned and sized ahead of grading.

stages.title: Grading & Cupping
stages.desc: Sorted by screen size and density, then cupped by trained tasters to verify quality and grade.

stages.title: Export Preparation
stages.desc: Bagged, documented and compliance-checked, with full lot records prepared for shipment.

stages.title: Shipping
stages.desc: Containerized and shipped from the port of Djibouti to markets across the world.

questions.a: Our minimum order is 1 MT, and a full container load is about 19.2 MT — priced FOB.
We supply Specialty, G1, G2, G3 and G4 grades, each cupped and graded before it's offered.

questions.q: Which ports do you ship to?
questions.a: We ship FOB Djibouti to Rotterdam, Jeddah, New York and Shanghai, serving 4 regions overall — USA, Europe, the Middle East and Asia.
Lead time is typically 18–40 days depending on the destination port, confirmed once your lot is selected.

questions.q: Do you offer private label or roasted coffee?
questions.a: Yes — private label and roasted coffee in food-grade packaging, alongside our core green coffee export.

questions.q: What quality checks do you do?
questions.a: Every lot passes five checkpoints — at station, drying, hulling & grading, cupping and shipment prep — plus international grading standards and full traceability records.

questions.q: How do I get a quote?
questions.a: Use the Instant Quote calculator on our homepage — pick a grade, volume and port for an indicative FOB price — or I can connect you with our export desk.
